Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
> Juggernaut1981 wrote:
> Cloak the Gathering is a legal play by a ready tapped which is not the acting minion but is controlled by the same Methuselah?
>
Sure. Being untapped is not (in the Rulebook) a requirement for playing action modifiers (which would scarcely be used, if it were the case).

Cloak the Gathering
[Jyhad:C, VTES:C, Sabbat:C, SW:C, FN:PS3, CE:C/PM4, BH:PM4, Third:PM6, LotN:PS2, KoT:C, HttB:PSam4]
Cardtype: Action Modifier
Discipline: Obfuscate
[obf] +1 stealth.
[OBF] Only usable by a ready vampire other than the acting minion you control. The action gets +1 stealth.

Some action modifiers require an untapped vampire. In these cases, the wording is explicit. Perhaps the Golden Rule of Cardtext should also read "If a card doesn't contradict the rules, then follow the Rulebook"..

Name: Veil the Legions
Cardtype: Action Modifier
Discipline: Obfuscate
[obf] Only usable by a ready, untapped vampire other than the acting minion you control. The acting minion gets +1 stealth. Only one Veil the Legions may be played each action.
[OBF] As above, and this vampire may burn X additional blood to give +1 stealth to the next X actions your minions perform this turn. Only one Veil the Legions can be played at superior each turn.

Name: Mask of a Thousand Faces
Cardtype: Action Modifier
Discipline: Obfuscate
[obf] Only usable by a ready, untapped vampire other than the acting minion who is capable of performing the action. Not usable if any action modifiers or other effects have been used that could not have been used if this vampire were the acting vampire. Untap the acting minion and tap this vampire instead. The action continues with this vampire as the acting minion.
[OBF] As above, with +1 stealth.

Messages.Author: Soonerborn
Messages.Body:
It wasn't my question but I often ask 'dumb' questions (that I already know the answer to) either because the situation arose during play and resulted in a disagreement or sometimes preemptively to avoid a potential future arguemeent when I intend play some esoteric combo or deck idea. Getting an 'official' ruling upfront is never a bad idea. Even at the cost of condescending banter from the vekn board...

I know I personally have attempted a legal play and had it essentially not accepted by the rest of the table (voted down?). The situation hadn't arisen before and all the other players decided it wasn't legal. But it was legal per LSJ. It wasn't tournament play so there was no official judge to make the call.

But that's no guarantee. It's been many years now but my brother got hosed by a wrong call in the final of a tourney that pretty much cost him a shot at the win. The judge for the event (who I won't name but is definitely 'famous' within the vtes community) had much more experience with competative play yet he made the wrong call.

Being a gentleman he later apologized for getting the ruling wrong but the point is that sometimes you get fucked. Not everybody has played countless games and encountered every scenario, that's why I think questions get asked that others might deem as obvious. JMO.
